html:
The refugees who fled Vietnam by sea in small, crowded boats after the fall of Saigon in 1975. Almost 800,000 reached other countries by 1995, and many others died at sea.

The new communist government sent hundreds of thousands of people with ties to the old regime to re-education camps, seized businesses and pushed families into new farm zones. Ethnic Chinese Vietnamese suffered most, above all during the 1979 war with China, and they made up a large share of those who fled.

The boats headed for Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Hong Kong. Storms, thirst and pirates in the Gulf of Thailand killed many. The death toll is unknown but ran to tens of thousands at the least.

A 1979 conference organised by the UN refugee agency led Western countries to resettle large numbers. The United States took the most, followed by Australia, Canada and France. Later arrivals were screened, and the last camps closed in the 1990s. The refugees built communities abroad and spread Vietnamese food such as phở around the world.
sum: The refugees who fled Vietnam by sea in small, crowded boats after the fall of Saigon in 1975. Almost 800,000 reached other countries by 1995, and many others died at sea.
